title: Rotate Right
statement:
A carousel has seats holding the numbers in `nums`. When it turns once, every number moves one seat to the right, and the last number wraps around to the first seat.

Return the list after the carousel turns `k` times. `k` can be larger than the length of the list.

examples.explanation: The last 3 numbers move to the front.
Two turns move 3 and 99 to the front.

hints.nudge: Turning n times (the list length) brings everything back. So how many turns really matter?
hints.pattern: Use k mod n, then reverse parts of the list.
hints.pseudocode:
k = k % n
reverse the whole list
reverse the first k elements
reverse the remaining n - k elements
hints.walkthrough: Doing k single turns costs O(n*k), far too slow for k up to a billion. First reduce k to k % n, since n turns change nothing. Then the answer is the last k elements followed by the first n - k elements. In place, you can get this with three reversals: reverse everything, then reverse the first k, then reverse the rest. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
